meta_description: A summarized list of necessary and specific agendas for the non-binary community, from ABRANB consultations and debates.

topics.title: Access to civil registration
items: Name rectification and sex mention as “non-binary” or another self-determined option other than male/female on the birth certificate and all other personal documents, in a streamlined way, without requiring reports, payment, or court proceedings;
Updating all digital systems and institutional forms to add this new option;
Speeding up pending court cases for document rectification of non-binary people.

topics.title: Access to architecture and the city
items: Updating building codes and sanitary code drafts and laws that recommend/require restrooms for only "2 sexes/genders", so that they guide architectural solutions for these spaces without gender segregation or exclusion, since they are currently, on this topic, inconsistent with the federal constitution, with the legal-state recognition of non-binary people, and with human rights and gender identity treaties to which Brazil is a signatory;

Construction of genderless restrooms (for all people), with toilets in secure, closed, individualized stalls, without exposed urinals. And/or renovation of existing restrooms into restrooms without gender segregation;
De-binarization of spaces generally segregated by the gender binary, through renovations of existing facilities or the provision of new facilities.

topics.title: Access to health and the "gender-affirming" process
items: Training for health providers to deal with non-binary people, in reception and communication;
Inclusion of social name, pronouns, and non-binary gender mention in health system records for registering and updating the records of patients who so identify;

Explicit inclusion of gender non-binarity in CFM resolution No. 2,265/2019, which regulates the "gender-affirming" process, expressly naming non-binary people as subjects of rights to all procedures to which other trans people are entitled;
Free access to hormones, psychiatric medication, and surgical procedures of the "gender-affirming" process through the public health system (SUS);
Strengthening and expanding trans outpatient clinics into the interior, with
multidisciplinary staff who truly address the physical and psychological needs of non-binary people and trans people in general, without absurd wait lists;
Public gyms for free physical exercise practice by non-binary people and LGBTQIAPN+ people in general;
Access to gender-neutral restrooms in psychiatric hospitals, CAPS (psychosocial care centers), and other health units;
Access to dignified psychological and psychiatric treatment without asylum-based violence, recognition by the CFP, CRM, and other bodies regarding the inclusion of gender-neutral language;
Free provision of all items needed to overcome menstrual poverty for non-binary people (and other people who menstruate) at health units, reference centers, and trans outpatient clinics;
Education and oversight strategies for the abolition of all obstetric violence in medical practice against non-binary bodies and others capable of gestating;

Decriminalization and legalization of abortion for non-binary people and others capable of gestating, as a guarantee of the right to self-determination and bodily autonomy, to overcome deaths in clandestine clinics and terminations performed under precarious conditions - a public health imperative.

topics.title: Access to work and income
items: A national training, income, and employment policy with a budget commensurate with the size of the non-binary and trans population in general (4 million people), aimed specifically at this population;

Universal basic income, without prejudice to existing social programs, consistent with meeting the social rights set out in Article 6 of the federal constitution, also considering the absurd rise in the cost of living during the pandemic;
Application of quotas in public and private employment consistent with the non-binary and trans population in general (2% of positions), with incentives for those who hire this population;
Combating labor discrimination against non-binary and trans people in general, with public campaigns and sanctions for companies that fail to act against or favor transphobia;
Federal education program in public and private companies on gender diversity, with paid hiring of non-binary and trans people to raise awareness among corporate staff;
Repeal of the labor reform and reduction of the workday without reducing wages.

topics.title: Access to education free of binarism and transphobia
items: Ensure the use of social name and personal pronouns at school;
Ensure access to all activities and spaces within the school for non-binary people of all ages, without gender segregation, whether they are students, teachers, or staff;
Ensure permanent curricular spaces addressing the fight against binarism and LGBT+phobia in general, racism, and sexism, as well as the integration of these topics into existing subjects;
Quotas for non-binary and trans people in general, at a minimum percentage matching this population's proportion of the Brazilian population (2%), in public universities and federal institutes;
Ensure the social right to education by eliminating the entrance exam (vestibular) as a criterion for admission to free public universities;
Repeal of the new high school curriculum proposed by the BNCC.

topics.title: Access to housing
items: Budget for the installation and maintenance of collective/community houses self-managed by the non-binary and trans population in all states of the federation;

Comply with Article 6 of the federal constitution, which guarantees housing as a social right, ensuring housing is provided for the non-binary and trans population in general in places worthy of living, whether by funding rent or by expropriating properties that fail to fulfill their social function and directing them to this purpose.

topics.title: Access to data, information, and media
items: Data collection on the non-binary population, with public funding for sociodemographic and clinical surveys concerning the non-binary population in Brazil, preferably hiring people from this population to conduct this research;
Inclusion of alternatives to male/female sex/gender in the IBGE census, offering at least the "non-binary" option;

State advertising in public or private media making non-binary and trans people in general visible, whether by hiring communicators from these groups or by directly addressing the topic of gender diversity;

A transparency portal for the federal LGBTQIAPNB+ department, accessible online by anyone, providing all data on the public budget allocated to the department, as well as a general and detailed description of expenses from the application of this budget for maintaining institutional positions and direct activities benefiting the LGBTQIAPNB+ population.

topics.title: Access to land and permanence on the land
items: Expropriation of rural land that fails to fulfill its social function and the granting of public land to LGBTQIAPNB+ people who are victims of domestic and family violence, homeless LGBTQIAPNB+ people, and those unemployed and in economic precarity in urban centers;
A program to provide and fund tools, seedlings, and agroecological seeds for rural LGBTQIAPNB+ people;
Cistern programs and other techniques for access to water for human consumption and community farming, coordinated by LGBTQIAPNB+ people;
Programs with a commensurate budget to enable rural housing, including multi-family housing for the shelter and self-management of LGBTQIAPNB+ people;

Strengthening the preventive health system and health in general in rural areas, with community medicine, psychotherapy, and the availability of STI testing and medications linked to the "gender-affirming" process for non-binary and trans people in general;

Demarcation of indigenous lands with the reclamation of territories by ethnic groups, and of quilombola communities, as well as funding for the projects of non-binary and LGBTQIAPNB+ indigenous and quilombola people in villages, quilombos, and urban centers.

topics.title: Access to justice
items: Expansion of human rights units within public defender's offices through staff hiring, and the establishment of a specific LGBTQIAPNB+ unit to overcome the current shortfall in supply relative to demand;
Online legal services at public defender units and reference centers, to reduce bureaucracy and cost for non-binary and trans people;
Free legal assistance for non-binary and trans people in general;
Training on gender and non-binarity in security officer training, especially regarding the treatment and approach of the LGBTQIAPNB+ population;
End of mandatory military service, for non-binary people whether or not their documents have been rectified, and for everyone else.

topics.title: Access to budget for non-binary and trans community projects in general
items: Public calls for proposals with budget for projects addressing poverty, hunger, housing precarity, and LGBT+phobia, and for the cultural, physical, and mental health promotion of non-binary and trans people in general.

topics.title: Access to protection and dignity regarding the prison system
items: Establishment (in existing prisons) of LGBTQIAPNB+ wings, with their own restrooms and without building new prisons;
Provision of basic hygiene and clothing items to incarcerated non-binary and LGBTQIAPNB+ people in general, especially those without family ties or support;
Access to trans outpatient services for incarcerated non-binary and trans people who require psychotherapy and hormone therapy;
Decarceration policies for LGBTQIAPNB+ people, with job and income training and agreements with public and private companies for hiring LGBTQIAPNB+ survivors of incarceration.

topics.title: Access to personal and collective recognition in language
items: Respect for any grammatical treatment claimed by people, regardless of their gender identities and expressions;
Training for service staff in public and private spheres in the proper use of grammatical alternatives, both without and with neolanguage;
Inclusion of teaching on gender grammatical alternatives, both without and with neolanguage, in linguistic and social subjects at public and private institutions;
Legal recognition of neolanguage as part of individuality and the right to personality;
Acceptance of neolanguage in all spheres as a reflection of language and a phenomenon of total importance for the social recognition of non-binary people and gender dissidents in general;
Suspension and repeal of all bills seeking to prohibit the use, application, and circulation of neutral and de-binarized forms of language in public space, media, and public and private institutions.
